evidence: The central route and parsing choice is largely supported: A1, A4 and A5 document Bearer-authenticated chat-completions routes, A2 and A3 supply compatibility caveats, and B1-B4 justify a fail-closed local check rather than assuming portable strict-schema support. B5 and B6 support caution about self-preference, and the 10%/25% figures match B5, but they do not establish a cross-family benefit for this dossier-validation task. The refutation section is operational in part, yet its automatic parsing switch and family-rule conclusion do not follow cleanly from the proposed observations.
gaps: A1 does not by itself verify the host-specific claim that one OpenRouter key covers every family in the model map; neither that map nor per-model endpoint support is shown.

Two validators across this dossier plus five more produce 12 calls. Specify that the trigger is a failure rate above 10%—therefore at least two failures in 12—and classify failures: B1 and B4 show that strict json_schema cannot cure refusals, incomplete output or truncation, so a failure count alone does not justify switching to option 3.

The single planted-error experiment has no same-family comparator and cannot show that the family rule 'buys nothing'; it tests whether one validator and brief detect one error. Use repeated planted errors and comparable same-family versus cross-family validators.

The recorded A3 claim does not support the usage-token citation, and Rejected overstates A3 as 'test-only' rather than primarily intended for testing and comparison. B5 supports avoiding pairwise position bias, not eliminating every possible position effect.
